Prayer times

On this page
  • Open the prayer times
  • What the Times view shows
  • See another day
  • The Chart view
  • Change how the times are calculated

Taqwim computes the five daily prayers for your place, together with sunrise and sunset, and counts down to the next prayer. This chapter explains the prayer screen and the settings that change the times.

Open the prayer times

  1. On the home screen, tap Calendar.
  2. A new installation opens on the Prayer times mode. If another mode is shown, tap the mode's name in the coloured title bar and choose Prayer times, or step with the double arrows on either side.
  3. Make sure Times is selected under the title bar.

To open Taqwim straight on the prayer times, set Settings → App → Start screen to Calendar, and Settings → Calendar → Open Calendar on to Prayer times.

What the Times view shows

From top to bottom:

  • The day bar: the date shown, with arrows for the previous and next day. When another day is shown, a Today button brings you back.
  • The dates panel: the Hijri date and the Gregorian date. The Solar Hijri date and the Julian Day can be added in Settings → Prayer.
  • The clock: the time now at your place, labelled Time now when today is shown.
  • The two boxes (today only):
    • Since and the prayer whose time has begun, with the time that has passed since it began;
    • the next prayer followed by in, with the time left until it in hours and minutes, for example "Asr in 01:24" (with seconds when Show seconds is on).
  • The times: Fajr, Sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, Sunset, Maghrib and Isha. The current prayer is highlighted. Sunrise and Sunset are dimmed because they are not prayers.
  • The method line: for example "Calculation method: Umm al-Qura". When you use the Hanafi Asr time, the line says so too. When two places or two devices show different times, this line usually tells you why.

Under it is the month calendar. Tap any day to see its times.

Sunrise marks the end of Fajr's time. Between Sunrise and Dhuhr, the Since box therefore keeps counting from Fajr.

A dash (—) in place of a time means that the event does not happen at your place that day. This happens far from the equator; see High-latitude rule below.

See another day

  • Tap the arrows in the day bar, or tap a day in the month calendar.
  • Tap the month title above the calendar to open Choose a date: turn the day, month and year wheels (in the Gregorian, Hijri or Solar Hijri calendar), then tap OK.
  • When the calendar shows a day other than today, a bar names it (Showing:) with Back to today.

The Chart view

Tap Chart under the title bar to see the Sun's height through the day:

  • the hours of the day across, and the Sun's altitude in degrees up, with the Horizon at 0°;
  • night, twilight and daylight as coloured bands;
  • each prayer marked on the curve with its name and time;
  • the Sun's place now, with Sun's altitude now and its azimuth under the chart;
  • the next prayer and its countdown, for example "Next: Maghrib in 02:05".

Calculation methods

The methods differ mainly in how far the Sun must be below the horizon at Fajr and Isha. Choose the one your local mosque or authority follows. At the first launch, and when you move to another country, Taqwim suggests the method in the right-hand column.

Asr time

  • Standard (the majority opinion: Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali): Asr begins when an object's shadow equals its length, plus the shadow it had at noon.
  • Hanafi: Asr begins when the shadow is twice the object's length, plus the noon shadow. Asr is then noticeably later.

High-latitude rule

Far from the equator, in summer, the Sun may not go deep enough below the horizon for the Fajr and Isha angles, or it may do so very late. The rule decides what happens then:

  • None: a time that the Sun never reaches stays missing and is shown as a dash.
  • Middle of the night: Isha is never later, and Fajr never earlier, than half the night from sunset and sunrise.
  • One seventh of the night: the same, with one seventh of the night.
  • Angle-based (default): the share of the night follows the method's angle (the angle divided by 60).

Taqwim never shows a made-up time without telling you: with None you see a dash, and with the other rules the times follow the rule you chose.

Rounding and seconds

  • None keeps the seconds.
  • Nearest minute rounds each time to the closest minute.
  • Precautionary rounds Sunrise down and every other time up, so you never pray before the time or end Fajr too late.

Turning Show seconds on also switches Nearest minute to None, so the seconds mean something; turning it off switches back. A Precautionary choice is left as it is.

Use elevation

When on, Taqwim takes the place's height above sea level into account in its calculations. Set the elevation in Settings → Location → Edit by hand. Leave it off unless your local times are computed for the elevation too.

Time offsets

Use Time offsets in minutes to match a local timetable exactly. Tap − or + beside a prayer to move it by one minute, up to 30 minutes either way. The offsets also move the alerts.
